parts.name: Anterior band
parts.attachment_or_location: anterior thickened rim, continuous with the superior head of lateral pterygoid
parts.function_note: the lateral pterygoid's superior head inserts partly onto this band, giving the disc a degree of active positional control unusual among fibrocartilaginous structures.
parts.source: Bag AK, Gaddikeri S, Singhal A, Hardin J, Wadhwa V, Chen J, Guillerman RP (2014) 'Imaging of the temporomandibular joint: an update.' World J Radiol 6(8):567-582 -- TMJ disc position, band anatomy, and internal derangement correlation.

parts.name: Intermediate zone
parts.attachment_or_location: thin central zone between the anterior and posterior bands
parts.function_note: the thinnest part of the disc and the primary load-bearing zone interposed between condyle and articular eminence during function.
parts.source: Bag AK, Gaddikeri S, Singhal A, Hardin J, Wadhwa V, Chen J, Guillerman RP (2014) 'Imaging of the temporomandibular joint: an update.' World J Radiol 6(8):567-582 -- TMJ disc position, band anatomy, and internal derangement correlation.

parts.name: Posterior band / bilaminar (retrodiscal) zone
parts.attachment_or_location: posterior thickened rim, continuous posteriorly with the vascularized bilaminar retrodiscal tissue
parts.function_note: unlike the avascular disc proper, the retrodiscal tissue behind this band is richly vascularized and innervated -- the classic anterior-disc-displacement pattern in TMJ internal derangement loads this normally non-load-bearing, pain-sensitive tissue.
parts.source: Bag AK, Gaddikeri S, Singhal A, Hardin J, Wadhwa V, Chen J, Guillerman RP (2014) 'Imaging of the temporomandibular joint: an update.' World J Radiol 6(8):567-582 -- TMJ disc position, band anatomy, and internal derangement correlation.

function: A biconcave fibrocartilaginous disc dividing the TMJ into separate superior (gliding/translation) and inferior (rotation) synovial compartments, whose anteroposterior position relative to the condyle is the key finding in TMJ internal derangement / disc displacement.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); Bag AK, Gaddikeri S, Singhal A, Hardin J, Wadhwa V, Chen J, Guillerman RP (2014) 'Imaging of the temporomandibular joint: an update.' World J Radiol 6(8):567-582 -- TMJ disc position, band anatomy, and internal derangement correlation.
